note:
CHIEF COMPLAINT
Runny nose, nasal congestion, cough, and ear pulling.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient is a 5-year-old male with symptoms that started around supper time last night. Guardian reports runny nose with clear mucous and nasal congestion. Patient has a cough that is not barky. Guardian notes patient has been pulling on ears and rubbing nose. Rectal temperature was 100.3°F. Appetite variable—ate well last night, consumed about 7 ounces from bottle this morning and barely finished another bottle, refused cereal. Patient is energetic but irritable and having difficulty sleeping. Exposure history: older sister is sick; recent play date with nephew who had a sinus infection. Home treatments attempted: saline mist to nose, Tylenol given early this morning due to body sweating, Baby Vick's on feet last night, humidifier used.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Runny nose with clear mucous, nasal congestion, cough (non-barky), ear pulling, nasal rubbing, low-grade fever, decreased appetite, irritability, difficulty sleeping, energetic but fighting sleep. No barky cough noted.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Cradle cap, recently worsening.

MEDICATIONS
Tylenol (given this morning), saline mist nasal drops, Baby Vick's, humidifier use.

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Older sister currently sick with similar symptoms.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Recent play date with nephew who had a sinus infection.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Lungs: Clear to auscultation bilaterally, excellent air movement. Ears: Appear normal. General: Well-appearing child.

RESULTS
Viral upper respiratory infection suspected. No evidence of bacterial infection at this time.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Viral upper respiratory infection. Plan: Continue fluids and rest. Monitor closely for development of barky cough. If barky cough develops, administer sister's cough medicine at half teaspoon dose for five days. Zarbee's cough syrup for regular cough using pediatric dosing for children under one year of age. Avoid honey; use agave instead. Avoid Honey Nut Cheerios. For cradle cap: Use dandruff shampoo (Head & Shoulders, Selsun Blue, or Nizoral AD regular strength, not extra strength) twice weekly with soft brush and baby oil to remove scales; continue for approximately six weeks. Avoid contact with eyes during rinsing. No antibiotics at this time. Follow up in one week. Return sooner or call if symptoms worsen, particularly if barky cough develops. If condition worsens, notify clinic.
